candidate.answerReason: The 6 empty chairs are one-fourth of the chairs, so 18 people are seated. Those 18 people are two-thirds of the total, giving 27 people.

methods.label: Find the size of one fractional share
methods.explanation:
Since \(\frac34\) of the chairs are occupied, the \(6\) empty chairs are the remaining \(\frac14\). Each quarter of the chairs therefore contains \(6\) chairs, so the three occupied quarters seat
\[
3\cdot6=18
\]
people.

These \(18\) seated people make up \(\frac23\) of all the people. One-third of the people is therefore \(18\div2=9\), and all three thirds contain
\[
3\cdot9=27
\]
people. The answer is \(27\), choice D.
methods.levelReason: The solution reconstructs whole quantities through equal fractional shares using only integer multiplication and division.

candidate.annotationRationale: The target is recovering a whole from a known fractional part, first for chairs and then for people. The method uses the unit-share interpretation of fraction-division applications. Fraction meaning supports keeping the two different wholes clear.
